Fatherless
fä´ther-les
n., adj. (without a father; rendering Hebrew yathom)
Father with the privative ending. The fatherless in Israel's law are a protected class, and God repeatedly names Himself their relative.

Biblical Definition

The fatherless are those without a father. God takes the title personally: “A father of the fatherless, and a judge of the widows, is God in his holy habitation” (Psa 68:5). The law forbids afflicting them and attaches a terrible warning (Exo 22:22–24). Deuteronomy leaves the forgotten sheaf and the gleanings for them (Deu 24:19–21), and James defines religion by them: “Pure religion and undefiled before God and the Father is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction” (Jas 1:27).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines fatherless as destitute of a living father; as a fatherless child; and without a known author.

expand to see more

FATHERLESS, a. Destitute of a living father; as a fatherless child.

2. Without a known author.

FATHERLESSNESS, n. The state of being without a father.

Key Scripture

Psa 68:5 — "A father of the fatherless, and a judge of the widows, is God in his holy habitation."

Exo 22:22 — "Ye shall not afflict any widow, or fatherless child."

Jas 1:27 — "Pure religion and undefiled before God and the Father is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep himself unspotted from the world."

Deu 24:19 — "When thou cuttest down thine harvest in thy field, and hast forgot a sheaf in the field, thou shalt not go again to fetch it: it shall be for the stranger, for the fatherless, and for the widow: that the LORD thy God may bless thee in all the work of thine hands."

Modern Corruption

Care for the fatherless is treated as one charitable option among many, and James makes it half of the definition of undefiled religion.

expand to see more

James 1:27 does not say visiting the fatherless is a good work; it says it is what pure religion is: pure religion and undefiled before God and the Father is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep himself unspotted from the world. Two halves, and neither is optional. A community rigorous about the second half and absent on the first has kept half a definition and called it obedience.

Psalm 68:5 explains why the duty is so heavily weighted: a father of the fatherless, and a judge of the widows, is God in his holy habitation. God does not merely command care for them; He identifies Himself by the relation. Exodus 22:23-24 states the consequence with unusual heat — if thou afflict them in any wise, and they cry at all unto me, I will surely hear their cry; and my wrath shall wax hot.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew yathom (H3490), an orphan, fatherless; Greek orphanos (G3737), orphan — the word Christ uses in John 14:18, I will not leave you comfortless.

expand to see more

Hebrew yathom (H3490) — fatherless, orphan; Exodus 22:22, Deuteronomy 24:19-21, Psalm 68:5.

Greek orphanos (G3737) — orphan, comfortless; James 1:27, John 14:18.

Hebrew almanah (H490) — widow; the constant companion term.

Usage

"“A father of the fatherless… is God in his holy habitation” — the relation claimed."

"“To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction” — half the definition of religion."

"“My wrath shall wax hot” — the consequence of afflicting them."
